# AL-Swati Contracting (شركة السواتي للمقاولات)

> Stone cladding contractor in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with experience since 1994. AL-Swati supplies and installs mechanically fixed natural stone (mainly Riyadh limestone), marble, granite and porcelain facades, and installs the steel substructure behind them to the engineer's design, using its own direct workforce. 5-year written workmanship warranty attested by the Chamber of Commerce, issued by the contracting company.

Key facts (updated 26 November 2026):

- Experience: 500+ projects of experience since 1994 in Riyadh: villas, commercial towers and institutional buildings.
- Workforce: 100% direct workforce. AL-Swati's own team installs every facade under a site supervisor; installation is not subcontracted.
- Services: natural stone cladding (Riyadh stone, limestone, sandstone, granite), marble cladding, and large-format porcelain facades, for exterior facades and interior feature walls. AL-Swati does not do flooring, floor tiles or paving.
- Fixing systems: Up-Down angle brackets, PEN (pin) fixing, vertical C-Channel rails, kerf rail system and undercut anchors. Brackets and angles are stainless steel or hot-dip galvanised steel according to the project specification; anchor and bolt sizes follow the engineer's calculation and the consultant's specification. AL-Swati installs systems from Hilti, fischer and Rockany and local or imported accessories, as the project specification names; product approvals belong to the manufacturer and are submitted with the material submittal. Undercut experience: Hilti undercut anchors on 30 mm natural stone and on 20 mm porcelain. No panel is bedded on cement mortar.
- Engineering: design is by the project engineer or consultant. AL-Swati either installs to approved shop drawings supplied by the consultant or main contractor, or appoints an independent facade engineer for the project, who prepares the design basis, wind loads per the current SBC 301, calculations for the steel substructure, shop drawings and a part list, and visits the site weekly on those projects. Panel thickness: natural stone typically 30 mm, thicker on demand; marble and granite often 20 mm (exterior 20 mm panels on edge fixings need the engineer's check and stone tests, or an undercut system); porcelain per the panel maker's system.
- Submittals and warranty: material submittals and samples; mock-up on request; anchor pull-out tests on request, arranged with the anchor manufacturer or a testing laboratory and witnessed by the consultant; 5-year written workmanship warranty attested by the Chamber of Commerce, issued by the contracting company.
- 2026 price ranges in Riyadh (SAR per m², supply and installation on Up-Down brackets for a villa facade, excluding 15% VAT): Riyadh white stone 230-280, Riyadh limestone beige/yellow 290-375, granite 265-340, travertine and marble 505-700, large-format porcelain 265-340. C-Channel, kerf and undercut systems cost more; final prices follow a free site visit and a written quote.
- Service areas: all of Riyadh, including Al Malqa, Al Narjis, Hittin, Al Yasmin, Diriyah and Al Olaya, plus Dammam and Al-Ahsa.
- Contact: phone and WhatsApp +966 51 182 6313, email info@al-swaticontracting.com, office 7663 Abi Al Thaka St, Al Malaz, Riyadh 12842-3667. Sunday to Thursday, 08:00-18:00.
